row.why: For 'different than' he used من (thinking comparative); Amal gave عن and confirmed it at 32:21, and he ended with الهواء هون غير عن الهواء هناك. Engine wrote بعيد / بيد for غير: Amal never rejected the word and praised بعيد عن الهوا هناك with ممتاز.

row.why: سنان is a different word (teeth); Amal recast سنين and at 36:25 asked 'What's سنان?' (he: teeth). The 36:17 repeat is the same moment.

row.amal_said: إيش يعني عجل؟ ... عجا كتير الصباح؟ إيش يعني؟ ... Tell me it was very strong.
row.why: Engine wrote أجو; Amal's echo عجا = أجا (came). 'The wind came a lot' made no sense to her: she asked إيش يعني twice and steered him to كان قوي. She never raised number, so his 'it's singular' was his own guess - not B18.
row.english: the wind was very strong this morning

rulings.why: Her echo shows the singular أجا; her problem was the meaning of the verb, so vocab tier 1, not grammar B18.
Not an error: a bare time noun as an adverb (الصبح / الصباح) is normal Levantine - Amal herself said الصبح بكير at 18:50 - and she answered Nice.

row.amal_said: So you could either say my favorite stone or my favorite using عندي. المفضل عندي. ... Never takes pronoun ending.
row.why: مفضل is an adjective: it takes el- and never a pronoun ending (Amal 54:46 'المفضل is an adjective', 54:56 'Never takes pronoun ending'); standalone 'my favorite' is المفضل عندي.
row.english: the second stone was my favorite

rulings.why: A7 fits: Amal's whole fix is 'treat المفضل as an adjective' (the same frame as agreed A29); the pronoun-ending part goes in bucket2 A4. No new rule needed.

row.amal_said: مش هون. مش، مش في. مش هون. ... في is not is. في is there is.
row.why: For 'isn't here' he used في (there is) - the wrong word; Amal said 'مش في. مش هون' and 'في is there is'. His negation (مش) was fine, so it is not C4.

rulings.why: The fix is a word swap (في -> هون) with her meaning explanation; the negator was not the problem.
